title: Construct this triangle and draw its altitude
description: The sides are checked to make a triangle, then the base and two compass arcs build it. A set square slid along the base draws the altitude from the top corner, and a ruler measures it.
teaching_notes: One idea: build the triangle from its three sides with arcs, then draw the altitude with a set square slid along the base. Watch for students who measure a slanting side instead of the perpendicular.

source: Construct a triangle ABC with BC = 5 cm, AB = 6 cm, CA = 5 cm. Construct an altitude from A to BC.
video_script.why: The child can check three sides, name the kind of triangle and draw an altitude, and now does all of these in one construction.
video_script.substitution: Check the three sides, draw the base, cross two arcs for the top corner, then slide a set square along the base to draw the altitude.
video_script.anchor: triangle ABC with BC five centimetres, AB six centimetres and CA five centimetres
video_script.payoff_line: The altitude from eigh to bee cee is about four point eight centimetres

final_answer.value: Isosceles triangle ABC; the altitude from A to BC measures about 4.8 cm
final_answer.spoken: the altitude from eigh to bee cee is about four point eight centimetres

maths_rules: the longest side is less than the sum of the other two: 6 < 5 + 5 = 10, and the other two checks pass: 5 < 5 + 6 = 11
two sides are equal, BC = CA = 5 cm, so the triangle is isosceles
draw BC = 5 cm, an arc of radius 6 cm from B and an arc of radius 5 cm from C; they cross at A
slide the set square along BC until its upright edge touches A; AD is perpendicular to BC
AD measures about 4.8 cm, which is shorter than the slanting side CA of 5 cm
video_script.design: The triangle is built on the board in the anchor band. The base is drawn first, the two arcs cross at A, and the set square slides along the base to draw AD, which is then measured with a ruler.
